assets.prompt:
Use case: compositing.
Asset type: revised square game app icon, 1024 x 1024, opaque.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the fox icon. Image 2 is the actual forest lake background asset used by the game. Image 3 is actual game graphics showing the Honeycomb belt and Copper Mechanisms side casings.
Make these specific corrections to image 1:
1. Replace all of the outer forest background with the supplied actual lake artwork from image 2. Reuse its turquoise water with soft caustic reflections, willow branches, reeds, mossy stones and water lilies, keeping the same painted detail and colors. Reframe the actual background for a square composition. Do not invent a different forest or lake.
2. Replace the gray plain conveyor with the prettier in-game Honeycomb conveyor from image 3: warm honey-gold segmented belt with delicate hexagonal linework, thin gold front trim, and rose-copper rectangular end casings with the shallow horizontal decorative seams seen in image 3. Keep the game's simple flat, restrained cel-shaded geometry. No invented ornate machinery or photorealistic metal.
3. Correct the particle-color continuity rigorously. Exactly three open buckets, left orange, middle warm cream, right teal. ALL particles above and inside each bucket must be the exact same hue as that bucket. Orange only into orange, cream only into cream, teal only into teal. No mixed or contrasting grains. Also correct the origin of each flow: the orange trail must visibly separate from orange cells at the bottom of the fox's left cheek, the cream trail from cream cells at the bottom of the muzzle, the teal trail from teal cells on the board's right side. Clear narrow white-backed channels below these matching-colored source patches so no trail appears to come out of green cells or a cream border. Preserve most of the fox picture. Each trail is composed of several SMALL FLAT SQUARE cells, not giant cubes. A small matching-colored accumulation can be visible inside each bucket.
Preserve the prominent recognizable fox pixel face, cream square board frame, three simple tapered HANDLELESS bucket shapes and the composition of image 1. Flat square pixels without beveled tile edges. No UI, no lettering, no numbers, no extra objects. Make this feel like the real game screenshots with upgraded framing, not a glossy 3D reinterpretation.

Use case: compositing.
Asset type: landscape game banner, 1600 x 940, opaque full bleed.
Image 1 is the source design to adapt into a landscape banner. Image 2 is the actual lake background asset from the game, to reuse for the background.
Recompose image 1 into a beautiful wide 80:47 landscape cover. Preserve exactly its square cream-framed fox pixel puzzle, three HANDLELESS buckets, honey-gold Honeycomb conveyor with rose-copper end casings, and overall simple 2D game rendering. Keep the board square and the fox face proportionate. Center the board and belt, filling almost all available height. Expand the actual lake artwork from image 2 into the side margins: turquoise water caustics, mossy stones, willow branches, reeds and pink/white water lilies, preserving its particular painted style and colors. No forest-tree background from earlier versions.
CRITICAL color continuity: exactly 3 streams into exactly 3 buckets. Left ORANGE square pixels from ORANGE fox-cheek cells into the ORANGE bucket. Middle CREAM square pixels from the CREAM muzzle into the CREAM bucket. Right TEAL square pixels from TEAL picture-background cells into the TEAL bucket. Each source point, every falling square and the fill inside its destination bucket must visibly match that bucket's hue. Clear narrow white-backed gaps below the matching-colored source patches where needed; no colored stream should appear to originate in green pixels or in the cream frame. Keep the fox mostly intact and recognizable. Use small flat square particles like the game, never spherical grains or 3D cubes. All three bucket openings clearly visible, each fill one color only.
Keep the supplied Honeycomb conveyor design, its delicate hexagonal linework, thin golden front strip and copper casings. No changes to the game objects besides adapting their placement for the wide canvas. No text, numbers, logos, buttons, coins, new objects, or watermarks.

Use case: compositing.
Asset type: square winter app icon, 1024 x 1024, full bleed opaque.
Create the WINTER counterpart of image 1 while using the real game's seasonal artwork.
Input image 1: layout and flat game-object rendering reference, the newly made lake/fox icon. Keep its compact readable square-icon composition with large square puzzle board above 3 buckets on a straight conveyor.
Input image 2: ACTUAL winter background artwork from the game, use this artwork for the outer backdrop, not a generic winter forest. Preserve its snowy evergreen branches, pine cones, red rowan berries and delicate pale blue frosty center, reframing it to square and showing the recognizable branches at the edges.
Input image 3: ACTUAL winter gameplay screenshot. Use its pixel mosaic of TWO SNOWMEN wearing RED winter hats and RED scarves as the puzzle inside the cream board. Recreate this game's snowmen art with chunky flat square pixel cells, not smooth illustration. Also copy the Winter Workshop conveyor visible in this screenshot: blue segmented belt with thin white snowflake patterns and matching icy blue rectangular end casings with restrained snowflake decorations, front ventilation grooves and simple flat shading. This is the chosen in-game seasonal conveyor, not a new machine design.
Replace the fox with the screenshot's winter snowmen, the lake backdrop with the supplied winter background, and the honey-colored belt with that blue snowflake conveyor.
Exactly three simple tapered open buckets with no handles, left RED, middle WHITE, right LIGHT BLUE. Use thin contrasting outlines so the white bucket reads clearly. Three SHORT streams of small flat square pixels connect the bottom of the picture to these buckets.
CRITICAL physical/color continuity: left stream separates from the RED scarf tail and every red particle falls into the RED bucket; middle stream separates from the WHITE snowman's body and every white particle falls into the WHITE bucket; right stream separates from the LIGHT BLUE picture background and every light-blue particle falls into the LIGHT BLUE bucket. Each stream's source patch, every falling particle, and fill inside its bucket must have the SAME color as that bucket. Recompose the lower picture slightly if necessary to expose those three matching source patches at the lower edge; small emptied patches show white backing. No red particles from blue background or white snow, no yellow or orange grains, no mixing streams.
Preserve the simple actual game sprite look and direct readability at icon size: mostly flat 2D buckets and belt, crisp square pixel picture, detailed painted backdrop from the supplied asset. No high-gloss 3D, no huge cubes, no handles, no text, no numbers, no UI, no extra items, no watermark.

initial_direction_prompts.icon:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset type: square app icon, 1024 x 1024, full bleed, opaque, no rounded outer mask.
Primary request: Create a new marketing icon for the exact game shown in the reference screenshots, much closer to the real game graphics than a glossy 3D advertising illustration.
Input images: Image 1 is the actual fox puzzle level and defines the orange fox pixel picture, flat bucket shapes and forest palette. Image 2 is the classic game screen and defines the gray teal conveyor and boxy side casings. These are visual references, not a request to reproduce the full screenshot UI.
Composition: Enlarge the recognizable front-facing orange fox mosaic from image 1 into a cream-bordered square game board occupying the upper two thirds of the icon. Leave the fox face readable and nearly complete. Beneath the board show a short straight gray-teal conveyor belt with visible slats and low rectangular side casings, like image 2. Exactly three large simple tapered open buckets stand on the belt: orange, cream, and teal. A few small SQUARE orange, cream and teal particles fall from matching parts of the bottom edge of the picture into their respective buckets. The falling particles must look like the flat square cells in the screenshots, not spherical sand grains or liquid. Small clean white gaps at the drained bottom edge convey the game mechanic.
Style: Faithful flat 2D mobile game sprite graphics with very restrained cel shading; simple outlined trapezoidal bucket bodies, dark elliptical openings and slightly lighter rims, absolutely NO handles, no embossed details. Coarse crisp square pixel mosaic in the board; smooth simple vector-like conveyor and bucket shapes outside it. Match the actual screenshots' restrained rendering instead of toy-like 3D rendering.
Backdrop: Soft pale sage and muted teal, with only a hint of the forest leaves from image 1 near the outer corners; keep the central game scene clear. Good contrast and legibility at small app-icon size. Tight confident framing, balanced cream, burnt orange, deep teal and blue.
Constraints: no words, no numbers, no title, no interface buttons, no coins, no sparkle effects, no hands, no extra game mechanics, no photorealism, no glossy 3D buckets, no bucket handles, no watermarks. Show one pixel-picture board, one belt and three buckets only.
initial_direction_prompts.banner:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Asset type: landscape game storefront banner, desired 1600 x 940 pixels (80:47 aspect ratio), opaque full bleed.
Primary request: Make a wide companion banner for this real pixel sand sorting game, using its actual graphics faithfully.
Input images: Image 1 is the approved visual direction for the new app icon, use its fox picture, color palette and recognizable simple objects for consistency. Image 2 is actual gameplay and is the authority for the flat 2D bucket shapes, pixel particle style and lush forest setting. Image 3 is actual classic gameplay and is the authority for the straight gray teal belt and rectangular side casings.
Composition: One large cream-bordered SQUARE pixel-art game board centered in the upper portion of the wide banner. Recreate the orange fox face mosaic from the references, almost intact and immediately recognizable. The board must remain square; do not stretch the fox face to fill the landscape canvas. Beneath the board, one straight horizontal slatted gray-teal conveyor with boxy end casings and three open tapered buckets: orange, warm cream and teal. Match the bucket shapes closely to actual gameplay: smooth simple outlined tapered sides, dark elliptical opening, colored rim, no handles. Three short loose trails of small flat square pixel particles fall into color-matched buckets from slightly depleted regions along the board's bottom. Retain white backing in the small cleared patches, fox face still readable. The board and conveyor together should fill most of the image height, with comfortable safe margins. Main action centered, leaves and trees extending into the wider left and right margins; no empty text area needed.
Style: Actual game aesthetic, crisp coarse pixel-art cells only INSIDE the board and in falling particles; simple restrained 2D cel shading for the buckets and conveyor, and a softly painted forest background like the gameplay screenshot. Preserve readable cream border, strong orange fox silhouette, blue and dark teal pixel forest within the board, cool sage-gray mechanical components. The background outside the board shows gentle green foliage, soft woodland light, tree trunks and small ferns near the edges, subordinate to the puzzle.
Constraints: no written text, no numbers, no logo, no HUD, no buttons, no ad badges, no coins, no hands, no toy-like glossy 3D surfaces, no handles on buckets, no round sand grains, no liquid, no extra boards, no extra characters, no invented game mechanics, no watermark. Produce a polished landscape banner that looks like this game's art, not an unrelated 3D render.
